paragraphs: My name is May, and I am eleven years old. I like English, and I love books. On Monday, I saw a poster on the wall of our school. It said, "Language Day. Saturday, the seventh of November. Place: the school library, across the field. Time: ten o'clock to two o'clock. Follow the path from the gate. Stories in both languages." The languages are Thai and English. My brother Pat read it too. Pat is eight, and he likes stories about animals.

"Can we go?" asked Pat. "Yes, we can," I said. Under the title, there was a small picture of a book and three lines. "Ten o'clock: Stories for small children. Twelve o'clock: Word games for everyone. One o'clock: A story in English." "I want to hear both languages," said Pat. "Then you must stay for the English story," I said.

That night, I wrote a short note to my friend Mia. "Dear Mia, Come to Language Day on Saturday. Meet us at the school gate at ten o'clock. Do not forget your book for the word game. Your friend, May" I gave the note to Mia on Tuesday. She said, "I will not forget!"

On Saturday morning, Mia and I met at the gate. Pat came with us, and he held my hand all the way. We walked along the path across the field. Teacher Kim waited at the door of the library. "Welcome," she said. We stayed for all the stories. Mia and I read a funny story about a cat. A poster tells us what, where, and when.
text.summary: May reads a poster for Language Day at the school library. She writes a note to ask Mia to come, and the poster tells what, where, and when.
